No certification is claimed anywhere in this repository. --- ## 00 — Executive Product Brief ### Identity **IVANNA OMEGA SUPREME** is a proprietary spatial-audio technology for any Android 13+ device. It is a native C++ DSP engine (NDK) inside a Kotlin/Compose application, built around a single fusion core that reconstructs a spatial scene from any stereo signal — without metadata, without multichannel source material, in one real-time thread. The product is named after Ivanna, the owner's daughter. ### Purpose To make any stereo recording sound as if it were produced in a real acoustic space — with externalisation, coherent bass, and a stable spatial image — on a phone, with measurable performance and fail-closed engineering. The ambition is a new way of listening: sound that adapts to the listener's brain and room, holophonic 360° projection, the hardware disappearing. ### Positioning IVANNA is a single-developer, measurement-driven audio product. It does not compete on catalogue, distribution or marketing spend — it has none of those. It competes on DSP mathematics, on verification discipline, and on autonomous self-improvement: the product detects its own defects, rewrites its own code under a multi-model council, verifies the rewrite with tests and CI, and publishes the release — all inside its own domain, under a fail-closed containment guard. ### Current state (honest) - **Latest published release: v2.5.444** (14 November 2026). APK only (Route A). No Magisk module installed anywhere; the development phone is clean after a factory reset. - **v2.5.445 is in development** on `main` (assistant LLM routing, voice control of DSP settings, autonomous GitHub bridge, multi-model council). Its CI is in progress; it is not yet released. - **Sales: 0 units. Revenue: $0.** The product has not been sold. The sales page exists; the payment path (Gumroad) is not yet connected. - **Two open defects define the current engineering agenda:** the sound is still reported as muffled ("bofo") after the v2.5.441 loudness fix, and Route B (the system-wide AudioFlinger effect) couples to the mixer but does not process audio. Both are documented as open, with their evidence, in §08 and §10. ### The IES-001 standard This repository is documented to its own internal standard: **IES-001 — Ivanna Engineering Standard.** *A unified framework for product documentation, technical architecture, acoustic validation and engineering governance.* Seven principles govern everything in this repository: 1. **Technical Accuracy** — nothing without foundation. 2. **Measurable Performance** — all relevant performance must be measured. 3. **Architectural Transparency** — architecture understandable and traceable. 4. **Reproducibility** — results verifiable. 5. **Engineering Consistency** — homogeneous criteria. 6. **Lifecycle Governance** — change and version control. 7. **Premium Experience** — visual and documentary excellence. --- ## 01 — Product Definition & Scope ### What IVANNA is - A **spatial-audio engine** (Route A, in-app): it takes any stereo stream — the built-in player (TIDAL, local files), or a capture of another app — and renders it through a single DSP chain (ORBE, HOLOS, Φ, Volterra, ASRC) in real time. - A **built-in player** (BridgePlayer): TIDAL inside IVANNA and local files, played at 100% through the full DSP chain — the clean listening path, with no duplicate audio. - An **AI assistant** (Gemini by default; OmniRoute as a free opt-in brain): it answers questions through a real LLM and controls DSP settings by voice. - An **autonomous self-repair system**: a multi-model council that proposes, critiques and arbitrates code rewrites, verified by tests and CI, published through a GitHub bridge — inside the IVANNA domain only, under a containment guard. - A **Magisk module** (Route B, system-wide): an AudioFlinger effect plus a daemon (`ivanna_asrcd`) that processes the real mixer output. **Currently paused: it couples but does not process (see §08).** ### What IVANNA is not - **Not open source.** Proprietary software of Luis Uriel Pimentel Pérez. All rights reserved. The repository is public (visible) but carries no open-source licence. Reproduction, distribution, modification or use without the author's express authorisation is prohibited. - **Not new physics.** Its components have precedents: spherical harmonics, Kirchhoff–Helmholtz, Volterra series, Greenwood. What is novel is the combination in a single real-time thread over arbitrary stereo — and the claim is exactly that, nothing more. - **Not "no PCM" and not "no Fourier".** The signal remains PCM in 128-sample blocks, and HOLOS works in STFT (hop 128 / FFT 512). Where this repository says "unified acoustic-neural field" or "neural loop", read *model*: the neural loop is identity without a real sensor connected, and the real sensor is the phone's microphone. - **Not a one-click miracle.** Every function has a switch, a range and a cost. With everything off, the legacy chain is bit-exact. - **Not a certified product.** No audio, software or security certification is claimed. Standards are cited as references (see §09). ### Intended applications - Critical listening of stereo music on headphones, speakers, USB DAC and Bluetooth (profiles per route). - TIDAL playback (HiRes over Wi-Fi, Lossless over mobile) through the built-in player. - Local file playback through the same chain. - Acoustic measurement and calibration of the listening room via the phone microphone (relative tonal balance, not absolute SPL). ### Functional limits - Android 13+ only. The Moto G85 is the development and test phone; it is not the product's target. - Route A processes only what the app captures or plays. It does not process phone calls or the system mixer. - The microphone sensor is uncalibrated: it measures relative tonal balance at the phone's position, not SPL at the ears, and is unreliable below ~80 Hz. - TIDAL full playback uses an unofficial endpoint (see §09 and `docs/TIDAL_CONTRACTS.md`): it works, it is outside TIDAL's terms, and it is revocable. - The neural loop has no real biometric sensor connected; without frames it is identity. --- ## 02 — Acoustic Science & Engineering ### 2.1 ORBE — Near-Field Spherical Binaural (v2.5.363) Classical HOA+HRTF works in the far field, at fixed distance. ORBE places **each ERB band (24) at a continuous azimuth and distance (0.15–2.0 m)** with a spherical-head model (radius 0.0875 m): ILD that grows as the source approaches, ITD by Woodworth, parallax by head-tracking. The scene is estimated from the recording itself, per band (ILD, IPD→ITD, coherence, DRR). No metadata. **Defaults (by owner directive, 2026-11-08):** amount 1.0, distance 0.35 m, aperture 1.0, proximity 3 dB, diffuse 0.5, head-tracking on when a pose is available. **ACTIVE by default.** | Measure (host, 48 kHz) | Value | |:---|:---| | THD+N, off | −153.45 dB @ 1 kHz (bit-exact) | | THD+N, on | −139.37 dB @ 1 kHz | | IMD | −156.04 dB | | Latency (algorithmic) | 10.7 ms | | Throughput | 23× real-time | | Tests | 21 host tests; the tests fixed 5 real bugs (the worst: a fixed tail inflated the output 2×/4×/8× at 96/192/384 kHz) | **Limitation:** it does not model pinna magnitude; only rotation parallax (yaw). ### 2.2 HOLOS — Single Acoustic-Field Operator (v2.5.364) The twelve legacy functions are not twelve different mathematics: the spatial operator is in every case an evaluation of the **acoustic Green function**; the nonlinear term is a **Volterra-series term**; dynamics/EQ/width is a **gain field** per band and instant. HOLOS evaluates all three in a single domain (STFT hop 128 / FFT 512, 24 ERB bands) from a single state vector per band. Every legacy module is a degenerate case of it (ORBE *is* HOLOS with K = identity and Γ = 1). $$Y_b(t) = G_b(s_b) \;\circledast\; \big[\, K_b(s_b) \cdot X_b(t) \,\big] \cdot \Gamma_b(s_b)$$ `G_b` unified Green · `K_b` per-band Volterra kernel · `Γ_b` single gain field. `amount = 0` is the legacy chain, bit-exact, 15 ms crossfade, fail-closed per term. Thermal shed in 4 tiers. **Defaults:** amount 0.5, distance 0.35 m, aperture 1.0, proximity 3 dB, diffuse 0.5, **harmonics 0.0 (K off by retune)**, warmth 0.5, dynamics 1.0, width 1.0, γ 1.0, RT60 0.34 s. **ACTIVE by default.** **Retune v2.5.369 (measured):** the harmonic term K dominates distortion — any harmonics > 0 fails −70 dB (0.5 / 0.05 → −53.7 dB). Only harmonics = 0 complies. With K = 0, the spatial render G and the field Γ stay active and clean (measurable spatial effect: −44.0 dB vs bypass). | Measure (host, 48 kHz) | HOLOS off | Old defaults | Retuned default | |:---|:---:|---:|---:| | THD+N @ 1 kHz / @ 100 Hz | −153.5 dB / — | −31.5 / −33.2 dB | **−94.0 / −79.6 dB** | | IMD (SMPTE) | — | −28.2 dB | **−159.5 dB** | | Throughput | — | — | 3.5× real-time (the 15–25× design estimate was disproved by measurement) | 38/38 HOLOS tests + 2 retune tests; the tests found 2 real bugs (Parseval scale, Welch-type coherence). **Honesty:** there is no new physics in HOLOS. What is novel is the unification in a single fail-closed real-time thread over arbitrary stereo. ### 2.3 Hyper-State Operator Φ (v2.5.369) A single sample-by-sample operator, **without block FFT or STFT**, fusing three state vectors into one unified gain: `Y(t) = x(t) + wet · [Φ(s_neuro, s_emf, s_field) · x(t) − x(t)]`. One `wet` (`hyper_amount`), one gain, one peak guard. `amount = 0` is **bit-exact identity**. Fail-closed: NaN or invalid state → bypass; never silences, never raises level. Output never exceeds input peak. **ACTIVE by default (`amount = 0.5`, Harman 2018 target).** **The three vectors:** **S_neuro(t)** — on-device NPE (cochlear model + LIF over real audio) + EEG/ABR/fNIRS interface; the NPE is a **model**, not a measurement of the brain. **Z_emf(t)** — real measurement only; without a real source it is **identity** (a phone has no electrical path: the 3.5 mm AUX is output-only). **W_acoustic(r,θ)** — field measured by the microphone: `error_db` per band drives Γ; `coherence` is the confidence weight. **Modes:** **MEASURED (2)** — valid, fresh `SensorFrame` (< 500 ms): Γ from measured `error_db` × coherence, ±9 dB/band. **APPROXIMATED (1)** — no `SensorFrame`: spectral balance of the signal itself, toward the target, **cut only [−3, 0] dB**, slow (200 ms); audible in Route A today and **not a room measurement**. **Off (0)** — bit-exact identity. **Real acoustic sensor (microphone):** AudioRecord UNPROCESSED, 48 kHz mono → FFT 8192 → 24 ERB bands → `SensorFrame` over a lock-free SPSC queue; converges in ~0.5–1 s. **Limitations:** microphone **uncalibrated** (relative tonal balance, not absolute SPL); measures the phone's position, **not the ears**; unreliable below ~80 Hz; most reliable ~100 Hz–6 kHz. Host throughput 280× real-time; 10/10 tests. **Elite target curves — and the warning that matters:** the default target is the **Harman AE/OE 2018 curve** (Olive, Welti & Khonsaripour, AES 2018). But Harman 2018 **is a headphone curve**: for measuring loudspeakers in a room, the physically correct preset is **3 (loudspeakers in a room)**. Correcting toward the wrong target with an uncalibrated microphone **can make the sound worse** — and that is exactly what the default does today with loudspeakers until ABX validates it. The default is not changed in this version (owner decision pending); it is written here, without softening. Presets: **0 · Harman 2018 (default)** · 1 · Harman elite-lean (−3 dB bass < 100 Hz) · 2 · Diffuse-field H&M (reference, not recommended) · **3 · Loudspeakers in a room** (flat anechoic +6.6 dB < 105 Hz, −2.4 dB > 2.5 kHz). **Bass ±3 dB** (`bassTrimDb`): preference varies widely (Olive 2025: the central 90% chose between +0.8 and +12.6 dB). The Harman value at 20 kHz (−17.1 dB) is an artefact and **is not used**. ### 2.4 Volterra kernel selector — PZ1D REFINED / GENEZI Atomic replacement with ~18 ms fade, persists across restarts; in Route B it applies on the next start. The kernel is measured from real hardware (GENEZI MHC-PZ1D); without a measured kernel, Volterra is identity. The selector, the `AuxVolterraGate` (only the measured IVK1 kernel passes, K=64) and the kernel-switch tests are in the repository. ### 2.5 NEU·Ω — Holographic Spectral Compiler (design by the owner) The whole chain compiles into one complex 2×2 matrix per band per hop; audio passes through the spectral domain once (L+jR packing, 257 unique bins); 2 FFTs per hop instead of 10; spectral latency 512 samples (~10.7 ms). **Status:** Phases 0, 1 and 2 complete and verified on host; **Phase 6 (live) is wired but OFF by default** (`neu_enabled`, fail-closed); Phases 3, 4 and 5 are pending. The design document is private and is not in this repository. | Check (host) | Criterion | Measured | |:---|:---|:---| | E1 (exact) | ≤ 1e-6 | passes | | E2 (broadband noise, ILD constant) | ≤ −80 dB | **−137.7 dB** | | E2/E3 (tones) | ≤ −80 dB | −142.24 / −142.29 dB, −143.67 / −143.77 dB | | E7 | ≤ −60 dB | passes | **Correction (by the owner, accepted):** the original "bit-identical 1e-6 vs serial" criterion was mathematically wrong — two serial STFTs with OLA are not equivalent to one multiplication in a single frame. The contract is now in dB (above). Isolated tones are not a valid E2; the broadband test is the valid one. ### 2.6 Ω — Universal Operator (v2.5.444) The equipment is a channel; Ω inverts what is invertible and moves any equipment toward the elite signature (Harman 2018 + Δ_b) without ever degrading. **v1, Route A only.** Profile N1 (no measurement): flat `H_b`, reinforcement capped at **+3 dB**. Crosstalk ceiling theorem: `D_max(κ) = −20·log10(κ)` (mono κ=1 → 0 dB: no binaural holophony, declared). Hierarchy Ω0 > Ω1 > Ω2 > Ω3. **OFF by default.** Auto equipment by real route (BT → E3, AUX/USB → E1, speaker → E2). Δ_b = 0 (gap #1, not invented). `K^Ω` = identity, `w_b` = 1 (open gaps, marked, not invented). 10/10 host tests (U1–U9 + N1 cap). Measurement by sweep (N2), measured `H_b` per equipment, Ω/Φ arbitration and Ω in Route B are future work. ### 2.7 ISO 226 loudness compensation The loudness compensation was found with its **sign inverted** (v2.5.441): the composite curve cut bass −12 dB and treble (12.5 kHz) −8.8 dB. The one-line fix (`lp(listen) − lp(ref)`) now gives **+9.4 dB @ 31.5 Hz, +7.6 @ 63 Hz, +5.5 @ 125 Hz, +3.2 dB @ 12.5 kHz, ~0 dB @ 4 kHz** (62→82 phon), verified numerically against ISO 226:2003 §A.1, with `Iso226CalibratorTest` (3 tests). **Honest status: the fix did not resolve the reported "bofo" sound** (see §08). The muffled sound is now hunted in Route A. ### 2.8 Closed-loop neural and NPE **Loop: wired, off by default, fail-closed.** `ClosedLoopController` + `NeuroBandEq` (8 Greenwood peaking biquads) run once per block **before** HOLOS/ORBE. Without frames, the loop is bit-exact identity. Ingest accepts only real EEG/ABR/fNIRS (the simulated sensor was removed) — but **no real sensor driver is plugged in yet**: without frames it does nothing audible. Cortical times are slow (ABR: 1000–2000 trials; fNIRS peaks at 6–8 s): the real design is a slow observer (100 ms–4 s) on a non-RT thread, never sample-by-sample brain correction. 11 host tests. Design in `docs/NEURO_ACOUSTIC_CLOSED_LOOP.md`. **NPE (neuromorphic engine, wired in the chain):** `NpeStereoCore` implements hair-cell models and leaky integrate-and-fire (LIF): cochlear bank + LIF pool + envelopes + OHC + AGC + lateral inhibition. Its "spikes" are triggered by the **audio envelope**, not the brain: today there is no biometric input. The NPE models the inner ear; it does not measure the listener's brain response. It is the on-device neural component: it runs on the phone's processor, with no external hardware. ### 2.9 Homogeneous Fusion Φ (v2.5.367) and pending pillars (v2.5.368) **Exist as classes with passing tests. NOT wired into the audio chain.** `HomogeneousFusion` fuses neural loop + AUX Genezi route + HOLOS into a single coordinator with a single state. 7/7 host tests. The pending pillars — diagonal Volterra K=4096, DoP v1.1, Blauert Pinna-EQ, EMF estimator — are components with passing tests (11/11) that are **not used**. A passing test is not an audible effect; this README does not confuse the two. --- ## 03 — Technical System Architecture ### 3.1 The two routes | | **Route A — APK (capture) · LIVE** | **Route B — Magisk + HAL · PAUSED** | |:---|:---|:---| | What it processes | Audio from the built-in player (TIDAL, local files) and capture of other apps | Nothing. Paused since 2026-11-11 | | Requirements | Install the APK only | Do not install any zip of any version | | Failure mode | If it fails, only the app falls | — | **Route B, measured 2026-11-13:** Effect ID 899 (UUID `4956414e-…`), TIDAL session 2169, Enabled, 1 track active — but `fusion_active=0`, `psi_active=0`, ratio 1.000000, drift 0.00, 0 mappings in audioserver. The effect couples to the mixer and passes audio through without processing. The phone is clean after its 7th factory reset; no module, no daemon, no Route B is installed. Route B returns only on a stable phone, with the `IvannaOmegaEffect` log naming the gate that cuts processing. ### 3.2 Signal chain (Route A) Real order in `IvannaFusionEngine::process()` (`app/src/main/cpp/IvannaFusionCore.cpp`). Each stage off is bit-exact. The neural loop runs once per block before HOLOS/ORBE. `IN → EvoEQ → HOA → HRTF → WFS → Neuro → ORBE → HOLOS → OmniField → Φ → AUX → T4D → user EQ → NPE → room correction → XTC → compressor/limiter → GoldenEar → OUT` (microphone → Φ) **Active:** HOA order 2 + HRTF (8 virtual speakers, max-rE) · WFS · ORBE (1.0) · HOLOS (0.5, harmonics 0) · AUX Genezi (XTC + coherent-phase AUX bass field) · GoldenEar (H2 off, soft-knee only) · Volterra H2 (PZ1D kernel) · compressor/limiter (threshold −12 dB, ratio 1:1, no reduction until configured) · parametric/evolutionary EQ (512 bands) · NPE · Φ (0.5, Harman 2018) · acoustic sensor · elite target curves. **Bypass/off:** RIR (wetDry 0) · neural loop (identity without frames) · cochlear · crossfeed ITD. **Not wired:** Phi fusion (367) and pillars (368). DSP budget 6.67 ms/block; shed governor at 85% (5.67 ms). Blocks of 128 samples, 8–384 kHz. Capture: foreground `mediaProjection`; DifferentialReinjector with comb guardian; reinjection latency measured ~130 ms. **The capture path has a known flaw:** the original TIDAL audio keeps playing at full level (no public API can silence it) while the processed copy is added at 0.60 gain — the two sum and comb-filter. float32 + gzip-9 | --- ## 04 — Audio Signal Processing ### 4.1 ASRC (sample-rate conversion) **Route A (live since v2.5.404):** native ASRC v6 (FIR 319 taps + Catmull-Rom + Ψ 64 taps/ear, 2048-phase × 319 table) fed by the `AudioTrackBufferPll` servo (Theil-Sen, ±500 ppm), replacing the 64-tap Kotlin resampler, with Kotlin fallback if the native code does not load. Ψ active since v2.5.405 (the app designs the taps with `PsiCore`); live 1 Hz telemetry since v2.5.407. **13/13 tests** (v2.5.404) and **31/31 tests** (v2.5.405, Ψ) on standalone host. AudioFlinger already resamples to 48 kHz before the app, so the ASRC is fine ppm correction, not 44.1→48 resampling. **ASRC core (daemon v2 / Route B, measured on host, v2.5.439):** 25/25 tests — drift residue +0.000/+0.001/−0.011 ppm, THD+N −86.00/−84.08/−83.15 dB, full ±500 ppm rail sweep worst case −80.83 dB, underflow 0, cost 3.59% of one core. The HAL route of the ASRC is dead with Route B; its history (PAL probe, −6.25 ppm live drift, ASRC v5) is in `docs/HISTORIA_RUTA_B.md`. **Route A ASRC (measured on host, v2.5.412):** THD+N −138.8 dB at ratio 1.0 / −95.0 dB at +100 ppm in 320-frame blocks. ### 4.2 The servo `AudioTrackBufferPll` (Kotlin): Theil-Sen estimator, ±500 ppm rail. Hold on starvation (underruns freeze the output instead of acting on a distorted queue; `pll_hold` counter in telemetry). Underruns invalidate the clock estimate for that interval. Full telemetry line at 1 Hz (`pll_tgt`, `pll_cap`, `pll_occ`, `pll_hold`). ### 4.3 TIDAL inside IVANNA (v2.5.416+) Built-in player, no redirections to the system player. OAuth PKCE login on TIDAL's page (tokens encrypted, password never stored), search, playlists, queue, playback through the BridgePlayer at 100%. Prefetch of the next track, bounded LRU cache (500 MB / 12 files), automatic quality (Wi-Fi → HiRes, mobile → Lossless), one retry, stream telemetry. Encrypted tracks do not play (no DRM bypass); delivered quality is always visible. **Contract (see `docs/TIDAL_CONTRACTS.md`):** the official TIDAL Developer Program gives catalogue and search — previews only, no full playback, non-commercial terms. Full playback in IVANNA uses the unofficial `playbackinfopostpaywall` endpoint with a PKCE client_id: it works, it is outside the terms, and it is revocable. Selling with full TIDAL in compliance requires a commercial agreement (honest probability given to the owner: ~1 in 10). The app is not yet registered on developer.tidal.com. ### 4.4 The assistant `IvannaAssistant` / `IvannaAssistantViewModel` / `IvannaGeminiAgent` / `IvannaAgentCore` / `OmniRouteOrchestrator` / `GeminiOrchestrator`. **v2.5.445 fixes the core finding:** open questions ("what is holophony and why does it feel different from normal stereo?") were intercepted by the local classifier (substring "normal" → FLAT_NEUTRAL, confidence 0.97) and answered with the canned line "I left the sound neutral, without colouration". The new `OpenQuestionRouter` (pure, deterministic) routes open questions **only** to the real LLM (OmniRoute if enabled, else Gemini) with live streaming; the local core handles only real DSP commands. If the LLM fails, the app says so clearly — never a canned line pretending to answer. **Voice control of settings (v2.5.445):** `VoiceSettingsControl` interprets orders ("set ORBE to 1.0", "raise HOLOS", "turn off Phi", "set the GENEZI kernel") and **applies them** through the existing setters/JNI, confirming the change. Covered: ORBE amount, HOLOS amount, Φ amount, Volterra kernel, ISO 226 on/off, Ω enabled + equipment. If it does not understand a setting, it says so and invents nothing. 35 new tests (16 router + 19 voice control). ### 4.5 OmniRoute — free LLM brain (v2.5.443) The app uses the OmniRoute gateway on the VM (Tailscale, `http://100.71.103.19:20128/v1`) as an alternative brain to Gemini: `OmniRouteOrchestrator` (OkHttp 4.12.0, same interface as `GeminiOrchestrator`, circuit breaker 3 failures / 30 s, timeouts 15 s / 30 s, SSE streaming), default model the `ivanna-free` combo, gateway API key encrypted in `SecureConfigurationManager` (EncryptedSharedPreferences). 00 — Executive Product Brief

Identity

IVANNA OMEGA SUPREME is a proprietary spatial-audio technology for any Android 13+ device. It is a native C++ DSP engine (NDK) inside a Kotlin/Compose application, built around a single fusion core that reconstructs a spatial scene from any stereo signal — without metadata, without multichannel source material, in one real-time thread.

The product is named after Ivanna, the owner's daughter.

Purpose

To make any stereo recording sound as if it were produced in a real acoustic space — with externalisation, coherent bass, and a stable spatial image — on a phone, with measurable performance and fail-closed engineering. The ambition is a new way of listening: sound that adapts to the listener's brain and room, holophonic 360° projection, the hardware disappearing.

Positioning

IVANNA is a single-developer, measurement-driven audio product. It does not compete on catalogue, distribution or marketing spend — it has none of those. It competes on DSP mathematics, on verification discipline, and on autonomous self-improvement: the product detects its own defects, rewrites its own code under a multi-model council, verifies the rewrite with tests and CI, and publishes the release — all inside its own domain, under a fail-closed containment guard.

    01 — Product Definition & Scope

    What IVANNA is

  • An **autonomous self-repair system**: a multi-model council that proposes, critiques and arbitrates code rewrites, verified by tests and CI, published through a GitHub bridge — inside the IVANNA domain only, under a containment guard.
  • A **Magisk module** (Route B, system-wide): an AudioFlinger effect plus a daemon (`ivanna_asrcd`) that processes the real mixer output. **Currently paused: it couples but does not process (see §08).**

  • **Not open source.** Proprietary software of Luis Uriel Pimentel Pérez. All rights reserved. The repository is public (visible) but carries no open-source licence. Reproduction, distribution, modification or use without the author's express authorisation is prohibited.
  • **Not new physics.** Its components have precedents: spherical harmonics, Kirchhoff–Helmholtz, Volterra series, Greenwood. What is novel is the combination in a single real-time thread over arbitrary stereo — and the claim is exactly that, nothing more.
  • **Not "no PCM" and not "no Fourier".** The signal remains PCM in 128-sample blocks, and HOLOS works in STFT (hop 128 / FFT 512). Where this repository says "unified acoustic-neural field" or "neural loop", read *model*: the neural loop is identity without a real sensor connected, and the real sensor is the phone's microphone.
  • **Not a one-click miracle.** Every function has a switch, a range and a cost. With everything off, the legacy chain is bit-exact.

    • Intended applications

  • Critical listening of stereo music on headphones, speakers, USB DAC and Bluetooth (profiles per route).
  • TIDAL playback (HiRes over Wi-Fi, Lossless over mobile) through the built-in player.
  • Local file playback through the same chain.
  • Acoustic measurement and calibration of the listening room via the phone microphone (relative tonal balance, not absolute SPL).

  • Android 13+ only. The Moto G85 is the development and test phone; it is not the product's target.

    • ---

    02 — Acoustic Science & Engineering

    2.1 ORBE — Near-Field Spherical Binaural (v2.5.363)

    Classical HOA+HRTF works in the far field, at fixed distance. ORBE places each ERB band (24) at a continuous azimuth and distance (0.15–2.0 m) with a spherical-head model (radius 0.0875 m): ILD that grows as the source approaches, ITD by Woodworth, parallax by head-tracking. The scene is estimated from the recording itself, per band (ILD, IPD→ITD, coherence, DRR). No metadata.

    Defaults (by owner directive, 2026-11-08): amount 1.0, distance 0.35 m, aperture 1.0, proximity 3 dB, diffuse 0.5, head-tracking on when a pose is available. ACTIVE by default.

    | Measure (host, 48 kHz) | Value |

    |:---|:---|

    | THD+N, off | −153.45 dB @ 1 kHz (bit-exact) |

    | THD+N, on | −139.37 dB @ 1 kHz |

    | IMD | −156.04 dB |

    | Latency (algorithmic) | 10.7 ms |

    | Throughput | 23× real-time |

    | Tests | 21 host tests; the tests fixed 5 real bugs (the worst: a fixed tail inflated the output 2×/4×/8× at 96/192/384 kHz) |

    Limitation: it does not model pinna magnitude; only rotation parallax (yaw).

    2.2 HOLOS — Single Acoustic-Field Operator (v2.5.364)

    The twelve legacy functions are not twelve different mathematics: the spatial operator is in every case an evaluation of the acoustic Green function; the nonlinear term is a Volterra-series term; dynamics/EQ/width is a gain field per band and instant. HOLOS evaluates all three in a single domain (STFT hop 128 / FFT 512, 24 ERB bands) from a single state vector per band. Every legacy module is a degenerate case of it (ORBE *is* HOLOS with K = identity and Γ = 1).

    $$Y_b(t) = G_b(s_b) \;\circledast\; \big[\, K_b(s_b) \cdot X_b(t) \,\big] \cdot \Gamma_b(s_b)$$

    G_b unified Green · K_b per-band Volterra kernel · Γ_b single gain field. amount = 0 is the legacy chain, bit-exact, 15 ms crossfade, fail-closed per term. Thermal shed in 4 tiers.

    Defaults: amount 0.5, distance 0.35 m, aperture 1.0, proximity 3 dB, diffuse 0.5, harmonics 0.0 (K off by retune), warmth 0.5, dynamics 1.0, width 1.0, γ 1.0, RT60 0.34 s. ACTIVE by default.

    Retune v2.5.369 (measured): the harmonic term K dominates distortion — any harmonics > 0 fails −70 dB (0.5 / 0.05 → −53.7 dB). Only harmonics = 0 complies. With K = 0, the spatial render G and the field Γ stay active and clean (measurable spatial effect: −44.0 dB vs bypass).

    | Measure (host, 48 kHz) | HOLOS off | Old defaults | Retuned default |

    |:---|:---:|---:|---:|

    | THD+N @ 1 kHz / @ 100 Hz | −153.5 dB / — | −31.5 / −33.2 dB | −94.0 / −79.6 dB |

    | IMD (SMPTE) | — | −28.2 dB | −159.5 dB |

    | Throughput | — | — | 3.5× real-time (the 15–25× design estimate was disproved by measurement) |

    38/38 HOLOS tests + 2 retune tests; the tests found 2 real bugs (Parseval scale, Welch-type coherence). Honesty: there is no new physics in HOLOS. What is novel is the unification in a single fail-closed real-time thread over arbitrary stereo.

    2.3 Hyper-State Operator Φ (v2.5.369)

    A single sample-by-sample operator, without block FFT or STFT, fusing three state vectors into one unified gain: Y(t) = x(t) + wet · [Φ(s_neuro, s_emf, s_field) · x(t) − x(t)]. One wet (hyper_amount), one gain, one peak guard. amount = 0 is bit-exact identity. Fail-closed: NaN or invalid state → bypass; never silences, never raises level. Output never exceeds input peak. ACTIVE by default (amount = 0.5, Harman 2018 target).

    The three vectors: S_neuro(t) — on-device NPE (cochlear model + LIF over real audio) + EEG/ABR/fNIRS interface; the NPE is a model, not a measurement of the brain. Z_emf(t) — real measurement only; without a real source it is identity (a phone has no electrical path: the 3.5 mm AUX is output-only). W_acoustic(r,θ) — field measured by the microphone: error_db per band drives Γ; coherence is the confidence weight.

    Modes: MEASURED (2) — valid, fresh SensorFrame (< 500 ms): Γ from measured error_db × coherence, ±9 dB/band. APPROXIMATED (1) — no SensorFrame: spectral balance of the signal itself, toward the target, cut only [−3, 0] dB, slow (200 ms); audible in Route A today and not a room measurement. Off (0) — bit-exact identity.

    Real acoustic sensor (microphone): AudioRecord UNPROCESSED, 48 kHz mono → FFT 8192 → 24 ERB bands → SensorFrame over a lock-free SPSC queue; converges in ~0.5–1 s. Limitations: microphone uncalibrated (relative tonal balance, not absolute SPL); measures the phone's position, not the ears; unreliable below ~80 Hz; most reliable ~100 Hz–6 kHz. Host throughput 280× real-time; 10/10 tests.

    Elite target curves — and the warning that matters: the default target is the Harman AE/OE 2018 curve (Olive, Welti & Khonsaripour, AES 2018). But Harman 2018 is a headphone curve: for measuring loudspeakers in a room, the physically correct preset is 3 (loudspeakers in a room). Correcting toward the wrong target with an uncalibrated microphone can make the sound worse — and that is exactly what the default does today with loudspeakers until ABX validates it. The default is not changed in this version (owner decision pending); it is written here, without softening. Presets: 0 · Harman 2018 (default) · 1 · Harman elite-lean (−3 dB bass < 100 Hz) · 2 · Diffuse-field H&M (reference, not recommended) · 3 · Loudspeakers in a room (flat anechoic +6.6 dB < 105 Hz, −2.4 dB > 2.5 kHz). Bass ±3 dB (bassTrimDb): preference varies widely (Olive 2025: the central 90% chose between +0.8 and +12.6 dB). The Harman value at 20 kHz (−17.1 dB) is an artefact and is not used.

    2.4 Volterra kernel selector — PZ1D REFINED / GENEZI

    Atomic replacement with ~18 ms fade, persists across restarts; in Route B it applies on the next start. The kernel is measured from real hardware (GENEZI MHC-PZ1D); without a measured kernel, Volterra is identity. The selector, the AuxVolterraGate (only the measured IVK1 kernel passes, K=64) and the kernel-switch tests are in the repository.

    2.5 NEU·Ω — Holographic Spectral Compiler (design by the owner)

    The whole chain compiles into one complex 2×2 matrix per band per hop; audio passes through the spectral domain once (L+jR packing, 257 unique bins); 2 FFTs per hop instead of 10; spectral latency 512 samples (~10.7 ms). Status: Phases 0, 1 and 2 complete and verified on host; Phase 6 (live) is wired but OFF by default (neu_enabled, fail-closed); Phases 3, 4 and 5 are pending. The design document is private and is not in this repository.

    | Check (host) | Criterion | Measured |

    |:---|:---|:---|

    | E1 (exact) | ≤ 1e-6 | passes |

    | E2 (broadband noise, ILD constant) | ≤ −80 dB | −137.7 dB |

    | E2/E3 (tones) | ≤ −80 dB | −142.24 / −142.29 dB, −143.67 / −143.77 dB |

    | E7 | ≤ −60 dB | passes |

    Correction (by the owner, accepted): the original "bit-identical 1e-6 vs serial" criterion was mathematically wrong — two serial STFTs with OLA are not equivalent to one multiplication in a single frame. The contract is now in dB (above). Isolated tones are not a valid E2; the broadband test is the valid one.

    2.6 Ω — Universal Operator (v2.5.444)

    The equipment is a channel; Ω inverts what is invertible and moves any equipment toward the elite signature (Harman 2018 + Δ_b) without ever degrading. v1, Route A only. Profile N1 (no measurement): flat H_b, reinforcement capped at +3 dB. Crosstalk ceiling theorem: D_max(κ) = −20·log10(κ) (mono κ=1 → 0 dB: no binaural holophony, declared). Hierarchy Ω0 > Ω1 > Ω2 > Ω3. OFF by default. Auto equipment by real route (BT → E3, AUX/USB → E1, speaker → E2). Δ_b = 0 (gap #1, not invented). K^Ω = identity, w_b = 1 (open gaps, marked, not invented). 10/10 host tests (U1–U9 + N1 cap). Measurement by sweep (N2), measured H_b per equipment, Ω/Φ arbitration and Ω in Route B are future work.

    2.7 ISO 226 loudness compensation

    The loudness compensation was found with its sign inverted (v2.5.441): the composite curve cut bass −12 dB and treble (12.5 kHz) −8.8 dB. The one-line fix (lp(listen) − lp(ref)) now gives +9.4 dB @ 31.5 Hz, +7.6 @ 63 Hz, +5.5 @ 125 Hz, +3.2 dB @ 12.5 kHz, ~0 dB @ 4 kHz (62→82 phon), verified numerically against ISO 226:2003 §A.1, with Iso226CalibratorTest (3 tests). Honest status: the fix did not resolve the reported "bofo" sound (see §08). The muffled sound is now hunted in Route A.

    2.8 Closed-loop neural and NPE

    Loop: wired, off by default, fail-closed. ClosedLoopController + NeuroBandEq (8 Greenwood peaking biquads) run once per block before HOLOS/ORBE. Without frames, the loop is bit-exact identity. Ingest accepts only real EEG/ABR/fNIRS (the simulated sensor was removed) — but no real sensor driver is plugged in yet: without frames it does nothing audible. Cortical times are slow (ABR: 1000–2000 trials; fNIRS peaks at 6–8 s): the real design is a slow observer (100 ms–4 s) on a non-RT thread, never sample-by-sample brain correction. 11 host tests. Design in docs/NEURO_ACOUSTIC_CLOSED_LOOP.md.

    NPE (neuromorphic engine, wired in the chain): NpeStereoCore implements hair-cell models and leaky integrate-and-fire (LIF): cochlear bank + LIF pool + envelopes + OHC + AGC + lateral inhibition. Its "spikes" are triggered by the audio envelope, not the brain: today there is no biometric input. The NPE models the inner ear; it does not measure the listener's brain response. It is the on-device neural component: it runs on the phone's processor, with no external hardware.

    2.9 Homogeneous Fusion Φ (v2.5.367) and pending pillars (v2.5.368)

    Exist as classes with passing tests. NOT wired into the audio chain. HomogeneousFusion fuses neural loop + AUX Genezi route + HOLOS into a single coordinator with a single state. 7/7 host tests. The pending pillars — diagonal Volterra K=4096, DoP v1.1, Blauert Pinna-EQ, EMF estimator — are components with passing tests (11/11) that are not used. A passing test is not an audible effect; this README does not confuse the two.

    03 — Technical System Architecture

    3.1 The two routes

    | | Route A — APK (capture) · LIVE | Route B — Magisk + HAL · PAUSED |

    |:---|:---|:---|

    | What it processes | Audio from the built-in player (TIDAL, local files) and capture of other apps | Nothing. Paused since 2026-11-11 |

    | Requirements | Install the APK only | Do not install any zip of any version |

    | Failure mode | If it fails, only the app falls | — |

    Route B, measured 2026-11-13: Effect ID 899 (UUID 4956414e-…), TIDAL session 2169, Enabled, 1 track active — but fusion_active=0, psi_active=0, ratio 1.000000, drift 0.00, 0 mappings in audioserver. The effect couples to the mixer and passes audio through without processing. The phone is clean after its 7th factory reset; no module, no daemon, no Route B is installed. Route B returns only on a stable phone, with the IvannaOmegaEffect log naming the gate that cuts processing.

    3.2 Signal chain (Route A)

    Real order in IvannaFusionEngine::process() (app/src/main/cpp/IvannaFusionCore.cpp). Each stage off is bit-exact. The neural loop runs once per block before HOLOS/ORBE.

    IN → EvoEQ → HOA → HRTF → WFS → Neuro → ORBE → HOLOS → OmniField → Φ → AUX → T4D → user EQ → NPE → room correction → XTC → compressor/limiter → GoldenEar → OUT (microphone → Φ)

    Active: HOA order 2 + HRTF (8 virtual speakers, max-rE) · WFS · ORBE (1.0) · HOLOS (0.5, harmonics 0) · AUX Genezi (XTC + coherent-phase AUX bass field) · GoldenEar (H2 off, soft-knee only) · Volterra H2 (PZ1D kernel) · compressor/limiter (threshold −12 dB, ratio 1:1, no reduction until configured) · parametric/evolutionary EQ (512 bands) · NPE · Φ (0.5, Harman 2018) · acoustic sensor · elite target curves. Bypass/off: RIR (wetDry 0) · neural loop (identity without frames) · cochlear · crossfeed ITD. Not wired: Phi fusion (367) and pillars (368).

    DSP budget 6.67 ms/block; shed governor at 85% (5.67 ms). Blocks of 128 samples, 8–384 kHz. Capture: foreground mediaProjection; DifferentialReinjector with comb guardian; reinjection latency measured ~130 ms. The capture path has a known flaw: the original TIDAL audio keeps playing at full level (no public API can silence it) while the processed copy is added at 0.60 gain — the two sum and comb-filter. The clean path is the BridgePlayer (100% processed, no double audio).

    No ABX blind listening test has been run yet. Until it is, "the effects are felt" is a recorded impression, not a result. The enemy is bias: +1 dB or knowing "this is the new one" produces more "wow" than any algorithm. The target is an ABX (16 trials, level-matched, LUFS ±0.2 LU: ≥ 12/16 correct and preference ≥ +15 points, replicated in two sessions) plus temperature in use.

    The perceptual goal is defined in five measurable dimensions, summarised in a VISCERAL index with an anti-cheat rule (it does not rise if any dimension falls more than 10 points): Envelopment (late IACC 0.4–0.6 at 0.5–4 kHz) · Apparent width (early IACC 0.6–0.8) · Externalisation (ITD/ILD error < 20 µs / < 1 dB; % "outside the head") · Bass impact (crest factor < 250 Hz preserved) · Clarity without fatigue (flatness 2–8 kHz ±2 dB; fatigue after long listening).

    The frontier — what could be genuinely new physics: (1) GENEZI — a per-band Volterra kernel measured from real hardware (falsifiable: it must predict THD/IMD of an unused signal with < 1 dB error per harmonic). (2) A psychophysical law of envelopment — a law with R² > 0.7 against new listeners' judgements would be publishable. (3) A near-field head + torso model (G = G_head · G_torso · G_shoulder, RT cost < 5% of HOLOS). None of this exists in code yet — except the first step, the Blauert PinnaElevationEq (v2.5.368), unwired.

    09 — Security, Reliability & Compliance

    9.1 Security posture

  • **Proprietary, protected.** Anti-piracy hardening (integrity, build hardening, R8, native and dex obfuscation, anti-debug / anti-tamper / anti-hook, fail-closed) is complete in Phases 1 and 2. Honest limit: absolute impossibility does not exist on a device the attacker controls. Details are not documented publicly.
  • **Fail-closed everywhere.** Invalid input, missing daemon, invalid ratio, NaN state, failed LLM, corrupt download — every one degrades to a safe state (passthrough, identity, offline, no offer). There is no bypass as a product (only a fail-closed safety net).
  • **FusionEngine never in `omega_create_effect`.** Its constructor does I/O (HRTF `.ihr1`, `agent_memory.bin` by mmap) and many plain-`new` allocations; if anything fails in audioserver, `std::terminate` kills the service and the phone bootloops (4th brick, 2026-11-11). Creation is now **lazy in `omega_process()`** (single attempt, `new (std::nothrow)`); on failure, passthrough, and audioserver stays alive. The heavy engine is created lazily on the first audio block — never at creation, never at dlopen.
  • **Secrets:** never in the repo, never in code, never in messages. The release keystore lives only as the CI secret `ANDROID_KEYSTORE_B64` (plus a backup outside the repo). API keys live in `SecureConfigurationManager` (EncryptedSharedPreferences) or in host-only files (mode 600). The auto-repair never touches credentials.
  • **Containment (autonomy):** the self-repair domain is ONLY IVANNA-OMEGA-SUPREME. Outside it, the guard blocks and reports. It never disables IntegrityGate, never touches credentials, never buys anything.

    • 9.2 Reliability

  • **No dangerous operations without the owner's explicit green light:** no audioserver restart, no reboot, no module swap, no install, no force-stop of IVANNA or another app, no change to another app's audio permission state. Default to read-only diagnostics.
  • **Route B is dead by design decision after the 6th factory reset** (HAL wrapper, v2.5.403 — never install, never retry). The wrapper cannot make init read a `.rc` at boot (init parses `/vendor/etc/init/` before Magisk mounts modules).
  • **Kill switches:** daemon `pal_asr.off` (no `c`); binary without `--kill` uses `pal_asrc.off` (with `c`); bridge `asrc.disable`. The 380 is the safe rollback.

    • 9.3 Standards — references, not certifications
